title: Giving and Verifying a Bluegate AutoPay Authorization: Tenant, Agreement, Account Holder and Verification Window
content:
## 1. Who gives the authorization

Only the tenant can authorize the Bluegate AutoPay Authorization. The care center records the authorization the tenant gives online, or on a recorded call where the method allows phone authorization, and sends the tenant a copy of the authorization by the method's copy delivery channel. Drafts run on the method's payment rail; an ACH authorization uses the method's online entry class when given online and its phone entry class when given by phone.

## 2. The agreement covered

The covered agreement must be, on the company's records, a Self-Storage Unit Rental Agreement in active, delinquent or moving-out status, or a Vehicle, RV & Boat Parking Agreement in active, delinquent, termination-noticed or moving-out status, and it must belong to the authorizing tenant. One authorization covers one agreement of a kind the method drafts (storage unit or parking).

## 3. The card or account

The card or account must be in the name the method requires (the tenant; the tenant or a joint holder; or the business on the customer profile), on a network the method accepts where it is a card, and the tenant's profile must be of the customer type the method requires. Prepaid and HSA or FSA cards are taken only where the method accepts them, and are refused otherwise. The account holder's name is taken exactly as the tenant states it; the customer type and the name or business name are those on the tenant's customer profile.

## 4. Verification

Until verified, the authorization is pending verification. Cards are verified at once by the method's verification method. Bank accounts are verified by micro-deposits, which must be confirmed within the method's verification window, with the method's allowance of wrong entries before verification fails. A verification may be completed only when the handling date is not later than the enrollment date plus the verification window. Window days are calendar days counted from the day after the enrollment date, and the last counted day is included. On verification the authorization becomes active and drafting starts. If verification fails or is not completed inside the window, the authorization is cancelled; the tenant may also withdraw it before it is verified.

| Handling date compared with the enrollment date plus the window | Verification |
|---|---|
| Earlier than, or on, the last counted day | may be completed |
| After the last counted day | may not be completed |

*Boundary cases (hypothetical, 5-day window).* Enrollment on the 3rd: the counted days are the 4th to the 8th. Completing verification on the 8th is in time; on the 9th it is not.

## 5. First due date drafted

The first due date drafted is the first due date that falls at least the method's verification cutoff (in calendar days) after the verified date; an earlier due date is paid by the tenant directly.

*Boundary cases (hypothetical, cutoff of 3 days).* Verified on the 17th: a due date on the 20th falls 3 days after and is drafted; a due date on the 19th falls 2 days after, is not drafted, and is paid by the tenant directly.
